subject: Data retention & on-demand erasure: residency, evidence, and audit logs
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2026-12-09T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on default retention and proof-of-deletion for EU data

Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. We're running our vendor risk review for the Redwood integration and have a couple of follow-ups from legal & infosec around what you keep by default (requests, model outputs, prompt artifacts) and how deletion requests are handled for EU-resident accounts. Specifically: 

- For hosted API customers in the EU region, what is stored by default for the life of a session vs what is persisted to logs? Do streaming tokens (partial responses) ever land in durable storage?
- If BrightBank requests deletion of all artifacts for a given account and timeframe, do you provide a machine-verifiable proof-of-deletion artifact (hashes/timestamps) we can attach to our audit?
- How do you handle third-party exports (manual exports, customer-initiated data dumps) — do those create a separate retention copy and what is the deletion path for them?

Our compliance team also asked for an example erasure runbook or template we can reference for audit. I've attached our RFI and highlighted the sections. Appreciate a short reply with pointers and a follow-up call if needed.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Security Reviewer, BrightBank

Attachment: BrightBank_RFI_20261209.pdf (stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention and proof-of-deletion for EU data

Elena — thanks, and great questions. High-level answers below; attaching our operational runbook and a deletion-proof template for your audit team to look at.

Summary answers (short):
- What we store by default: for Hosted EU accounts, we persist API request metadata (headers, timestamps, routing) and final request/response artifacts (complete prompt + final model output) to a short retention logs store by default (45 days). Streaming partial tokens are treated as ephemeral and do not persist to the durable logs store unless the request completes and the assembled final output is stored.
- Proof-of-deletion: we provide a deletion_proof CSV that lists deleted object IDs, deletion timestamps (ISO8601), and a SHA-256 digest of the object at the moment of deletion. That file is signed by our internal key and can be delivered to customers; sample attached.
- Exports: manual or customer-initiated exports create a one-off export artifact retained in the customer's export bucket. Exports are subject to the same retention rules and can be deleted on request — we record export artifact deletion in the same proof-of-deletion template.

More detail and caveats:
1) Streaming vs assembled outputs: continuous streaming responses are buffered in an in-memory stream layer; only the reassembled final response (what the SDK returns when the call completes) is considered for persistence. If the SDK makes an explicit "persist=true" flag or the customer uses our export pipeline, we will write the assembled object to logs/export buckets.

2) KV cache and intermediate model state: KV cache shards used to accelerate inference are ephemeral and do not get persisted to long-term storage. Snapshots of model weights or runtime tensors are never written to customer-accessible storage; we treat those as ephemeral process memory.

3) Deletion process & timelines: once we receive a validated erasure request (API call + proof of account ownership), our internal erasure workflow: 
   - Identify all objects matching the account/timeframe (logs, exports, cached artifacts) — automated indexing completes within 2 business days.
   - Execute deletions across primary stores and export buckets — typically completed within 5 business days.
   - Generate deletion_proof CSV + internal signature and provide to customer or upload to a pre-authorized audit Drive link.
   - For legal holds or regulatory exceptions, we'll flag the case and provide a separate timeline (these are rare).

4) Audit evidence: our deletion_proof.csv contains object_id, object_type (request/response/export), recorded_checksum (SHA-256), deleted_at, and deletion_request_id. We can also provide an HMAC-signed manifest if BrightBank prefers a shared secret verification flow.

Next steps: happy to run a quick 30-min call (I can include Kimberly) to walk the runbook. If you want, we can also provide a sample signed manifest for your SIEM ingestion.

Attachments: redwood_erasure_runbook_v1.pdf, deletion_proof_template.csv (stubs)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager — Data Controls
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-11T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention and proof-of-deletion for EU data

Elena — answering your follow-ups and surfacing telemetry details.

1) Example signed deletion_proof: attached sample (deletion_proof_template.csv) shows columns and a mocked signature block. In production we replace sample IDs with actual object_ids and include an internal signature header. If you want us to produce a redacted real-case sample from a non-production tenant we can do that under an NDA.

2) Client-side copies: as you noted, Redwood cannot force deletion of copies downloaded by customers or third parties. We do however record the issuance of an export in the artifact index and the deletion_proof includes an explicit flag: export_issued=true/false and export_artifact_id. That helps auditors show that an export existed and when it was removed from Redwood-managed stores.

3) Analytics & derived telemetry: we maintain a separate telemetry index that stores aggregated usage metrics (token counts, latency percentiles) and pointers to anonymized object_ids for debugging. When a deletion request targets raw persisted objects, we remove references to the object_id from debugging pointers and mark the telemetry row as "redacted"; aggregated metrics (e.g., total tokens used in a day) remain, but they are not queryable by the deleted object_id after erasure. In short: we keep high-level aggregates but remove identifiers that would allow re-associating records to deleted content.

4) Technical API notes for automated erasure: 
   - Endpoint: POST /v1/accounts/{acct}/erasure-requests with JSON body {"from":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","to":"2026-12-01T23:59:59Z","verify_token":"..."}.
   - Response: erasure_request_id + estimated_completion (ISO8601).
   - Proof retrieval: GET /v1/erasure-requests/{id}/proof returns the signed CSV artifact.

I've looped in Laura (observability) and Jonas (infra) to validate the telemetry redaction behavior. If you'd like, we can schedule a short tech deep-dive and share a redacted real artifact under NDA.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager — Data Controls
Redwood Inference

summary: BrightBank asked for clarification on what Redwood stores by default in the EU, how streaming tokens are handled, and whether Redwood can produce machine-verifiable proof-of-deletion. Karthik responded with retention windows (default 45 days for final artifacts), confirmation that streamed tokens are ephemeral, an outline of the erasure workflow and timelines (identify: 2 business days; delete: 5 business days), and a signed CSV-based proof-of-deletion artifact. Follow-ups covered sample proofs, export issuance recording, and telemetry redaction behavior. Next step: tech deep-dive and possible NDA for redacted sample proof.
